templates.pattern: Light passes through medium 1 (refractive index [N1]) into medium 2 (refractive index [N2]) then into medium 3 (refractive index [N3]). What is the effective refractive index from medium 1 to medium 3?
templates.explanation: The refractive index from medium 1 to 3 = n3 ÷ n1 = [N3] ÷ [N1] = [RESULT]. The intermediate medium n2 does not affect the overall ratio.

templates.pattern: An optical fibre has a core refractive index of [NC] and cladding refractive index of [NK]. What is the critical angle in degrees? (Use: sin C = n_cladding ÷ n_core. sin 30°=0.5, sin 45°=0.707, sin 60°=0.866, sin 42°=0.669, sin 48°=0.743)
templates.explanation: Critical angle: sin C = n_cladding ÷ n_core = [NK] ÷ [NC]. For TIR to occur, n_core must be greater than n_cladding.

templates.pattern: A thin converging lens of focal length [F] cm has an object placed [U] cm from it. What is the image distance v in cm? (Use: 1/v = 1/f − 1/u with real-is-positive sign convention, u is positive)
templates.explanation: 1/v = 1/f − 1/(-u) in real-is-positive. With u positive: v = uF ÷ (u−F) = [U]×[F] ÷ ([U]−[F]) = [RESULT] cm

templates.pattern: Two thin lenses of focal lengths [F1] cm and [F2] cm are placed in contact. What is the combined focal length in cm?
templates.explanation: For lenses in contact: 1/F = 1/F1 + 1/F2 → F = F1×F2 ÷ (F1+F2) = [F1]×[F2] ÷ ([F1]+[F2]) = [F1*F2] ÷ [F1+F2] = [RESULT] cm

templates.pattern: A lens has power [P1] dioptres and a second lens has power [P2] dioptres. They are placed in contact. What is the combined power?
templates.explanation: Powers of lenses in contact simply add: P_total = P1 + P2 = [P1] + [P2] = [RESULT] dioptres

templates.pattern: A glass slab of refractive index [N] and thickness [T] cm is placed in the path of light. What is the apparent shift of an image behind the slab in cm?
templates.explanation: Apparent shift = t − t/n = t(1 − 1/n) = [T] × (1 − 1/[N]) = [T] − [T/N] = [RESULT] cm

templates.pattern: A microscope has an objective lens of focal length [FO] cm and eyepiece of focal length [FE] cm. The tube length is [L] cm. What is the total magnification?
An astronomical telescope has objective focal length [FO] cm and eyepiece focal length [FE] cm. What is the angular magnification in normal adjustment?
templates.explanation: Angular magnification = FO ÷ FE = [FO] ÷ [FE] = [RESULT]×. A longer objective and shorter eyepiece gives higher magnification.

templates.pattern: Light of wavelength [L] nm is used in a double slit experiment. The slit separation is [D] mm and the fringe width is [W] mm. What is the distance to the screen in metres?
templates.explanation: Young's equation: λ = Wd ÷ D → D_screen = Wd ÷ λ = ([W]×10⁻³ × [D]×10⁻³) ÷ ([L]×10⁻⁹) = [RESULT] m
